sources._comment: Each subfolder of queue/ is one post: post.txt (or post.md) plus any image/video files to attach.
Replace YOUR-HANDLE with the handle of YOUR OTHER account. Set enabled=true to scrape your own posts (text + images reliable; video best-effort).
Extra LinkedIn account you own: replace YOUR-HANDLE, then set enabled=true. Optionally add a per-source 'reformat' block (see README/comments in reformat section).
X/Twitter timeline. First run `npm run login` and sign into x.com in the automation browser window, then set enabled=true. Retweets skipped; videos skipped (text+images only).
Instagram profile grid. First run `npm run login` and sign into instagram.com in the automation browser window, then set enabled=true.
Facebook page feed. First run `npm run login` and sign into facebook.com in the automation browser window, then set enabled=true. DOM anchors are best-effort; may need tuning after first live login.

Substack source: set 'url' to the publication (https://<name>.substack.com or its custom domain) — the feed is picked up automatically. Add one entry per publication. Articles are rewritten to short posts per the 'rewrite' block, with a source link.

Medium source: set 'url' to an author profile (https://medium.com/@handle) or a publication (https://medium.com/<publication>) — the feed URL is derived automatically. Add one entry per profile/publication.
Generic blog source for any non-Substack/Medium blog listing or RSS feed. Replace the URL, optionally set 'linkPattern'.

reformat._comment: Global reformat defaults applied to every candidate. Each source entry may carry its own 'reformat' object that overrides these keys for that source only (autoHashtags and style merge key-by-key).

schedule._comment: Day-wise posting hours, local to 'timezone'. 'weekday' = Mon-Fri, 'weekend' = Sat-Sun; each is hour-of-day 0-23 on the hour. Posts per day = that day's slot count x post.maxPerRun. Hours are wall-clock in 'timezone' (pick it in the dashboard Schedule tab); install-schedule.sh translates them to the Mac's local clock (exact minute/weekday) into a day-of-week calendar; re-run it after a DST change in either zone; run.js re-checks each wake against the day's list, so a dashboard edit applies on the very next tick even before the plist is regenerated. Off-schedule wakes skip posting AND engagement without opening Chrome. Add an off-grid hour here then re-run ./install-schedule.sh so launchd knows to wake for it. A legacy 'hours' array applies to both groups.

browser._comment: profileDir is where the automation's Chrome profile lives (log in once via `npm run login`). Keep headless=false: headless is far more detectable.

engagement._comment: Outbound engagement on OTHER people's posts, run independently every scheduled wake (not tied to your own posting). Targets: 'handles' = linkedin.com/in/<name> people whose recent activity is scanned; 'keywords' = filter the auto-refreshed home feed by these words. Set one or both. pickStrategy: 'top' = most-engaged, 'recent' = newest, 'topRecent' = most-engaged of the newest 10. maxPerRun: how many posts to engage per run (1 = 'only once'). commentMode: 'ai' = a short tailored comment from the free LLM in rewrite.llm (falls back to pool/fixed if there is no key or the free quota is spent), 'pool'/'fixed' = static, 'none' = like only. Each post is engaged at most once ever (tracked in the ledger). Configure it in the dashboard (Posting & limits tab).

template._comment: Structured post shape for substack/medium articles: heading, 3 numbered takeaways (each EXACTLY takeawayWords words, validated and regenerated until valid), 5 bullets with bold intro phrases, article-image status, source link, footer. takeaways/bullets/source/footer are fixed by the template; hashtagCount is how many content-relevant tags the article gets (pool unchanged). Set template.enabled=false for the old plain-summary shape.

rewrite._comment: Rewrites article sources (substack/medium) into structured posts. mode: 'auto' uses the LLM when a key is available, else the built-in extractive template builder (no API needed; word counts enforced exactly). FREE by default: OpenRouter with a ':free' model (key from https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys — no card). If the main model is throttled (429) or rejects, 'fallbackModels' are tried in order — free pools are shared, so momentary 429s are normal. Any OpenAI-compatible base url works: Google Gemini free tier, Groq, or local Ollama (set "noAuth": true, no key). The key is read at runtime from env REWRITE_API_KEY or the git-ignored file state/rewrite.key — `npm run llm:setup` writes it with hidden input, `npm run llm:check` verifies it without printing it. attribution appends the source link — keep it on: summaries with credit are safe curation, silent rewrites of others' articles are not.
